The existing project is a small pixel survival game "Little Ember". The user's request is a completely different game: "Semi realistic simulation sniper with changeable bullet ballistics and optional gamepad controls. Make the game have a difficulty curve and progression with different rifle types and upgrades."

So I should replace index.html with a new sniper game. Single-file HTML/JS/Canvas likely. Need to build a complete playable game with:
- Semi-realistic ballistics: bullet drop, wind, scope, range estimation, zeroing
- Changeable bullet ballistics (ammo types with different velocity, drag, drop, maybe bullet coefficient)
- Optional gamepad controls (Gamepad API)
- Difficulty curve & progression with different rifle types and upgrades
- Playable in browser with screenshot verification.

Let me think about the design. Canvas 2D, pseudo-3D sniper view? We can create a first-person scope view rendered with canvas: terrain silhouette, targets at distance, bullet trajectory simulation in 3D with gravity + wind + drag. Scope with mil-dot reticle, elevation/windage turrets (zeroing), range finder, holdover. That'd be a compelling "semi realistic simulation sniper".

Alternatively, side-view 2D ballistics with parabolic arc. The request says "semi realistic simulation sniper" — scope view with ballistics would feel more authentic. We can implement a 3D world projected into a first-person camera: targets at various distances and lateral offsets, terrain hills, trees, buildings. Render via 2D canvas with painter's algorithm using projected points. We need good visuals.

Plan:
- Three.js? No network dependencies likely; use canvas 2D with custom 3D projection. More controllable and self-contained.
- Use a camera with yaw/pitch, FOV zoom. Scope overlay. World consists of terrain (heightfield), trees, rocks, buildings, targets (humanoid silhouettes), with distances 150–1200 m.
- Bullet physics: position, velocity 3D; gravity 9.81; drag based on ballistic coefficient / ammo; wind vector; simulate in substeps at high frequency, not per frame only (simulate with dt ~ 0.002s). Compute trajectory and impact against ground/target.
- Zeroing: adjust scope elevation in MOA/mil. The reticle center corresponds to line of sight; bullet drop requires holdover. Provide zero range selector (100–800m) plus manual elevation clicks, windage clicks. Or use mil-dot holdover. Simpler: scope has adjustable zero distance via keys / UI; bullet impact relative to crosshair depends on that. Add a mildot reticle for holdover.
- Range finder: laser rangefinder key (R) gives distance to target under crosshair (with cooldown), and wind indicator.
- Bullet types changeable: e.g., .308 Match (stable), .338 LM (fast, flat, expensive), subsonic (slow, huge drop, quiet), AP/incendiary? "changeable bullet ballistics" – include ammo selection with different mass, BC, muzzle velocity, cost. Also maybe reload key and magazine.
- Gamepad controls: optional toggle; left stick aim, right stick fine aim, RT fire, LT scope/hold breath, bumpers adjust zero, D-pad select ammo, A reload. Show hints when gamepad connected.
- Progression: mission/campaign with waves or a series of contracts. Earn credits for hits (accuracy, distance, headshot bonus), spend on rifles (3-4 types: bolt-action trainer, .308 scout, .338 magnum, anti-materiel?) and upgrades (barrel, optic, stock, trigger, bipod, rangefinder). Difficulty curve: each mission increases target count, movement, smaller targets, wind, distance, time limit. Maybe "contracts" generated with escalating difficulty; each contract has 3 waves. Let's design:
  - Career mode with "Ops" (missions) numbered. Each op has a set of targets to neutralize (e.g., 4 + opIndex). Targets may patrol horizontally, some pop up and hide, some hostage? Avoid shooting civilians maybe complexity. Keep to hostile targets; add "no civilian" penalty? Could skip.
  - Difficulty: op index affects range, wind speed, target size/movement, time limit, target count, and precision required? Score bonus.
  - Between ops, Armory screen: buy rifles/ammo/upgrades with credits earned.
  - Persistent save to localStorage.

Need to make sure it actually runs and looks good. Screenshot via playwright. Check if playwright-cli exists.

Let me check environment tools and existing setup.

Also .omgithub/checkpoint.json may have instructions. Let's look.

Let me think through the visual rendering implementation carefully.

World 3D to 2D projection:
Camera at origin-ish (shooter position). Use yaw/pitch. World coordinates: x = lateral (right positive), y = up, z = forward distance. Camera at (0, height ~1.6, 0) looking along +z with yaw/pitch. For simplicity, targets placed at z = 200..1200, x = lateral offset, y ground height. Terrain: a heightfield along z with gentle hills, plus lateral variation. Camera position fixed. We can render:
- Sky gradient with sun, clouds? 
- Distant mountains silhouette.
- Terrain: draw strips/patches as projected quads? A full heightfield raster might be heavy but doable: sample terrain grid z from 50 to 2000, x from -800..800; project each cell and fill polygon. Painter's algorithm far to near. With ~120 z steps × 60 x steps = 7200 quads per frame — maybe okay but expensive in canvas 2D. Could reduce via LOD: 80 x 50 = 4000. Hmm.

Alternative: render terrain as a series of horizontal "hills" silhouettes based on height at z slices when looking roughly forward. But with yaw/pitch movement, a heightfield feels more 3D. Let's do a grid heightfield but optimize:
- Use terrain height function h(x,z) with smooth noise.
- Project vertices into screen. Only draw cells whose projected area is reasonable. Use z slices 40..1600 step maybe 20m near, 60m far? Lateral step scales with z to keep screen size consistent.
- Fill color based on distance fog and lighting.
That could work. Each frame we need projection of grid vertices; precompute grid vertices once per camera orientation; camera rotates with aim, so recompute. 4000 quads × 4 projections = 16k operations, fine at 60fps. Canvas fills 4000 polygons might be ~5ms? Could be okay. But when scoped (zoomed 8x), FOV small, most cells offscreen; cull fast. When unscoped, 70° FOV, we need enough coverage.

Maybe simpler and more visually striking: use a pseudo-3D scene rendered with pre-made layered art? But ballistics need targets at various depths, so true projection is better.

Let me design world visuals:
- Terrain height: base y=0 at ground; gentle rolling hills: h(x,z) = 2.2*sin(z*0.013)+1.6*cos(x*0.008+z*0.004)+... scaled. Sniper position elevated: camera eye at y=20 on a ridge overlooking a valley. Terrain heights vary -? Let's define ground height y=0 near shooter, valley dips maybe. Camera at y = 22, z=0. Targets at 300-1400m. Terrain visible as broad valley/hills.
- Add scattered trees (billboards: trunk + canopy polygons), rocks, buildings, watchtowers, fences, roads, grass tufts. Use deterministic random placement, project by z. Sort with targets by depth. Draw terrain first, then objects sorted far→near.
- Targets: humanoid shapes, simple but readable (head, torso, legs, arms), with colors distinguishing enemy. They walk along x within a range, stop, duck (crouch), peek. Some may be "on patrol" and move; others stationary. Hit zones: head (small, bonus), torso, limbs (less damage). Damage model: one-shot kill if head or torso for most; limb wound might require follow-up. Simpler: any torso/head hit kills; limb hit deals damage but target may run/hide. Bullet drop matters at range.

Rendering humanoid at distance: height ~1.7m. Project size: at 800m with 4x zoom FOV 15°, screen height ~? Use projection: screenY = H/2 - (y - camY)*f/z where f = (H/2)/tan(fov/2). With fov 15°, f = 270/0.1317 ≈ 2050. At 800m, 1.8m tall → 1.8*2050/800 ≈ 4.6 px. Too tiny. Real scopes at 800m: 1.8m subtends ~0.128°; if scope FOV 3° then ~1/23 of view = 40px. So max zoom should be much higher, like 12x-25x (FOV 2-4°). With 8x scope FOV maybe 5°, f = 270/tan(2.5°)=6183; at 800m → 14px. Still small. Actual 8x scope has FOV ~5°, human at 800m ~ 1/29 of height = 18px on 540px screen. Realistic. But for gameplay readability, targets need to be bigger; use distances 150-600m and zoom 6-12x. At 400m with FOV 4°, human = 1.8*7726/400 = 35px. Good.

Let's use ranges 120-700m, scope zoom 4x-10x. Unscoped FOV 65°, scoped FOV = 65/zoom roughly? Not physically exact but fine. At 6x, FOV ~11°, human at 400m → 1.8*(270/tan(5.5°))/400 = 1.8*2803/400 = 12.6px. Hmm too small. Let's set scoped FOV = 4.5° at 6x. Human at 400m → 1.8*6875/400=31px. Fine. Use scope zoom 5x with FOV 4.6°, 10x with FOV 2.6°, etc. Let's not overthink realism of FOV numbers; gameplay matters. We'll define scope FOV = 6° for 4x, 3° for 8x, 2° for 12x. At 500m, human at 8x = 1.8*(270/tan(1.5°))/500 = 1.8*10313/500=37px. Good.

Targets visible in scope only if within view; unscoped they're tiny but can be spotted by muzzle flashes or silhouettes.

The rifle sways; hold breath (Shift) steadies for a few seconds. Scope steadying based on stance/upgrades. Aiming with mouse movement maps to yaw/pitch; sensitivity scaled inversely by zoom. If we use pointer lock, aiming feels like FPS. Add pointer lock on click into canvas; mouse movement changes yaw/pitch. Escape exits. Alternatively click-drag to aim; pointer lock better for a sniper.

But screenshots and autoplay need no pointer lock issues. We'll support both: mouse move over canvas aims when pointer locked; when not locked, moving near edges? Simpler: clicking "Deploy" requests pointer lock. But browser screenshot will not have pointer lock; we can still show scene. We can also support drag-to-look without pointer lock (most robust). Use mouse drag to aim, with inertia-free direct mapping. Or use mouse position relative to center as aim offset? That's not great.

Better: hybrid: if pointer locked, relative movement; if not, click-drag rotates view. Keyboard arrows/WASD also aim. Aim assist? No.

Let me decide on control scheme:
- Mouse: move to look when pointer is locked (click canvas to lock). Without lock, drag to look.
- Left click / Space: fire.
- Right click / C: toggle scope? Actually right click hold to scope is typical. We can do right-click toggles scope (simpler for automation) or hold. Use right mouse down = scoped; release = unscoped. Also "Z" toggles scope.
- Shift: hold breath (steadies).
- R: rangefinder.
- Q/E or [ ]: elevation zero down/up; A/D? Those used for zero? Let's use arrow keys or comma/period for elevation, semicolon/quote for windage? Simpler: Elevation Up/Down keys = PageUp/PageDown, windage = Insert/Delete? Hmm.
- Zeroing could be automatic via "V" cycling zero ranges; and manual windage via "," "." maybe. For gameplay, provide a "ballistic solution" panel showing range, drop, wind drift, and suggested hold. Player can use mildots rather than fiddling with clicks. "Changeable bullet ballistics" via ammo selection keys 1-4.
- Add scope zero adjustment: keys `[` `]` for elevation (1 click = 0.1 mil?), `;` `'` for windage. And UI display. That's depth.
- Bipod/prone (X) reduces sway but maybe not needed.

Gamepad:
- Left stick: aim coarse; right stick: aim fine.
- RT: fire; LT: scope; RB: rangefinder; LB: hold breath? A: reload; B: cycle ammo; D-pad up/down: elevation; left/right: windage; Start: pause.
- Detect gamepad connected; poll in loop. Show "GAMEPAD CONNECTED" badge and hints. Optional controls: gamepad works alongside keyboard/mouse without toggling. That satisfies "optional gamepad controls".

Progression/armory:
- Rifles:
  1. "M24 Ranger" bolt-action .308 — starter, 5-round mag, muzzle 780 m/s, BC 0.45, zoom 4x, sway medium, reload 3.0s.
  2. "SR-25 Viper" semi-auto 7.62 — faster follow-up, lower velocity 760, 10 rounds, zoom 6x, more sway.
  3. "AX-338 Typhoon" bolt .338 LM — 900 m/s, BC 0.62, 5 rounds, zoom 8x, heavy, slower bolt.
  4. "M107 Wraith" .50 BMG anti-materiel — 850 m/s, BC 0.72, 5 rounds, huge recoil, can penetrate? zoom 10x, expensive. Maybe targets behind cover? Keep simple.
- Ammo types (changeable ballistics): Standard FMJ, Match (higher BC/consistency), Subsonic (300 m/s, massive drop, quiet, maybe only for close range), Armor Piercing (higher velocity, flatter, more damage), Tracer? Tracer helps see trajectory and adjust. Add specialty ammo purchasable per mission? Could make ammo inventory with counts? Simplify: each rifle has compatible ammo types selected by keys; all available after purchase in armory; infinite ammo per op but limited magazine. Bullet ballistics differ: muzzle velocity multiplier, BC, drop, wind drift.
  - Standard: MV ×1.0, BC ×1.0
  - Match: MV ×1.02, BC ×1.10, tighter
  - Subsonic: MV ×0.4, BC ×0.75, huge drop
  - AP: MV ×1.06, BC ×1.02, damage ×1.3
  - Tracer: visible trail, MV ×0.98, BC ×0.95 (helps aiming)
- Upgrades: Barrel (velocity +5%), Optic (zoom +, clarity), Stock (sway -20%), Trigger (spread/timing), Bipod (sway -35% when prone), Rangefinder (faster/accurate wind), Magazine (capacity +), Suppressor (reduces sway? no, maybe recoil).
- Credits earned per op; upgrade costs increase. Save progress.

Mission structure:
- "Operation" with target count. Start screen: briefing, deploy. In mission: HUD top left shows op number, targets remaining, time; bottom left ammo/rifle; top right wind/range; center scope overlay.
- Targets spawn at positions 200-700m based on op difficulty. Some patrol, some pop-up. Time limit. Each kill awards credits based on distance, headshot, time; misses maybe cost? End screen: "Operation Complete" with accuracy, credits, next op / armory.
- Difficulty curve: op 1: 3 static targets, 200-300m, wind 0-2 m/s, no time limit? op 2: 4 targets, 250-400m, wind 2-4; op 3: 5 targets with patrols and 400-550m; op 4: 6, 500-650, gusting wind; op 5+: 7+, farther, smaller exposure, moving, time pressure. Cap at e.g. 12 ops with escalating, then endless.
- To keep missions not tedious, target count moderate (4-8), shot resolution quick (bullet flight ~1s at 500m). Each mission ~2-4 min.
- Add wind gusts (sinusoidal + noise) and displayed average wind with indicator. Wind affects bullet; player must lead.
- Add breathing sway and heartbeat; hold breath meter.
- Add recoil that kicks view; scope re-acquire after shot. Bolt action delay.
- Add bullet cam? Maybe "kill cam" slow motion? Could add a tracer trace line and impact marker. Keep performance.

Rendering approach details:
Projection function:
```
const cam = {x:0, y:EYE_H, z:0, yaw:0, pitch:0, fov: scoped? FOV_SCOPED : FOV_HIP}
project(p) {
  // transform world to camera: translate then rotate yaw around Y and pitch around X
  let dx = p.x - cam.x, dy = p.y - cam.y, dz = p.z - cam.z;
  let cy=cos(yaw), sy=sin(yaw);
  // forward is +z, right +x. yaw rotates world? 
  let x1 = dx*cy - dz*sy;
  let z1 = dx*sy + dz*cy;
  let y1 = dy;
  // pitch rotation around x axis:
  let cp=cos(pitch), sp=sin(pitch);
  let y2 = y1*cp - z1*sp;
  let z2 = y1*sp + z1*cp;
  if (z2 <= 0.1) return null;
  let f = (H/2)/Math.tan(fov*Math.PI/360);
  return {x: W/2 + x1*f/z2, y: H/2 - y2*f/z2, z: z2, scale: f/z2}
}
```
Pitch sign: if pitch positive = look up? y2 = y1*cp - z1*sp; looking up, the horizon should move down, so point at y=0,z=1000 projects lower. With pitch>0: y2 = -z1*sp (negative for z1>0) → screen y = H/2 - y2*f/z2 > H/2 → lower. Yes look up moves horizon down. Good.

Yaw: if yaw>0 turning right, a point straight ahead (z=1000) gets x1 = -z1*sy <0 → left of center. Good.

Camera at (0, 18, 0) maybe on a ridge. Terrain height function:
```
groundH(x,z) = 
  14 + 9*Math.sin(z*0.0032+0.5) + 6*Math.cos(x*0.004+z*0.0012) + 3*Math.sin(x*0.011)*Math.cos(z*0.006)
```
Need camera on a high point looking down into valley. We can place camera at y=32 and terrain near at y=20 sloping down to y=0 at z=400-800 then rising hills at far. Let's build specific valley:
```
function terrainH(x,z){
  const base = 6 + 10*Math.sin(z*0.0025) ...;
}
```
Actually simpler to render visually: near foreground ridge at y≈camY-8; mid valley y≈ -5..4; far hills rising y up to 40. Use:
```
h = 3 + 4*sin(z*0.004+1.2) + 3*cos(x*0.006) + 2*sin(z*0.011 + x*0.004)
```
Camera eye at y = 12, z=0, so looking down at ground ~9m below. Targets ~1.8m tall; at 500m, horizon. Hmm, viewer elevated 12m means targets seen slightly from above; fine.

Better: camera on a ridge at y=25, foreground ground around 18, valley at z=300 y≈0, far hills rise to 30 at z=900. This gives depth cues. Height function:

let t=smoothstep(...)
h = 20 - 22*exp(-((z-320)/260)^2) + 14*smoothstep(500,1400,z) + rolling
```
Something like: at z=0: h≈24 (near ridge); z=350: h≈2 valley; z=900: h≈18 hills; z=1500: h≈30. Add lateral rolling hills 2-4m, plus noise. Camera eye = h(0,0)+2 = ~26. Targets stand on terrain.

Simpler: fixed grid 120 z × 90 x covering x ±(1600), z 20..2200. But near rows huge cells; far rows tiny. Use log spacing in z: z_i = 10 * (1.035^i) maybe. 120 rows. In x, step proportional to z. At near distance z=20, x span ±40 step 2; at far z=2000, x span ±4000 step 200. So cells are roughly screen-sized. This is like a perspective grid. Let's implement per-row: row z, halfWidth = z * 0.9 + 60 (to cover wider FOV), N columns maybe 80; but each row would have ~80*120 = 9600 quads. Fine maybe. Culling and offscreen skip reduces. Could use 64 columns. Each quad projected; if both z near and far, fill polygon. Coloring: base terrain color varying with height and distance fog. Add subtle stripes? Could compute sun shading from slope. Looks like low-poly terrain.

However, a filled quad at far z will still be small. Layering order: draw rows far→near so near covers far. Within a row, order doesn't matter much. Add depth fog by blending to atmospheric color.

Alternative: draw only silhouette: for each column x, draw ground profile? Since camera can pitch/yaw, not simple.

Let's implement grid. Rendering objects: trees, rocks, buildings placed with (x,z) and heights. Project base and top; draw billboard. Sorting by z descending and interleaving with target draw list. Terrain first (all), then all objects/targets sorted far→near. Targets behind hills would show through. To handle, use painter sorting of targets relative to terrain rows? Hard. Could use a depth buffer? Canvas 2D doesn't have z-buffer. ```
function project(x,y,z) {
  const cy=Math.cos(yaw), sy=Math.sin(yaw);
  const dx=x, dz=z;
  const x1 = dx*cy - dz*sy;
  const z1 = dx*sy + dz*cy;
  const cp=Math.cos(pitch), sp=Math.sin(pitch);
  const y1=y;
  const y2 = y1*cp - z1*sp;
  const z2 = y1*sp + z1*cp;
  if (z2 <= 0.05) return null;
  const f = focal();
  return {x: W/2 + x1*f/z2, y: H/2 - y2*f/z2, z: z2, s: f/z2};
}
```

function pollGamepad(dt) {
 const pads = navigator.getGamepads ? navigator.getGamepads() : [];
 const gp = [...pads].find(p=>p && p.connected);
 update badge;
 if (!gp || state!=='mission') return;
 const ax = gp.axes[0], ay=gp.axes[1], rx=gp.axes[2], ry=gp.axes[3];
 apply deadzone

 buttons edge detection for fire etc.
}

function swayOffset(t) {
  const breathFactor = holding && breath>0 ? 0.18 : 1;
  const lowBreath = breath<=0 ? 1.8 : 1;

}

.btn.primary:hover{background:linear-gradient(180deg,#ffdc8d,#d8a84f);color:#111a0f}
.btn.primary small{display:inline-block;margin-left:8px;font-size:9px;opacity:.7}
.btn.ghost{border-color:transparent;color:var(--dim)}
.btn.ghost:hover{color:var(--amber);border-color:var(--line)}
.btn:disabled{opacity:.3;cursor:not-allowed}
.btn:disabled:hover{background:rgba(18,28,19,.72);border-color:var(--line2);color:var(--text)}
.eyebrow{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:3px;color:var(--muted)}
.screen{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:20;display:none}
.screen.active{display:block}
.scrim{position:absolute;inset:0;background:linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(4,8,5,.96) 0%,rgba(4,8,5,.8) 34%,rgba(4,8,5,.22) 64%,rgba(4,8,5,.4) 100%)}
.scrim.top{background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(4,8,5,.9),transparent 40%,transparent 60%,rgba(4,8,5,.9))}

/* ---------- title ---------- */
#screen-title .title-wrap{position:absolute;left:6.5%;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);width:54%;max-width:700px;z-index:2}
.kicker{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:4px;color:var(--amber);text-shadow:0 1px 0 #000}
.kicker:before{content:"";display:block;width:38px;height:1px;background:var(--amber);opacity:.8}
#screen-title h1{font-family:var(--display);font-size:clamp(56px,9.4vw,118px);line-height:.78;letter-spacing:.5px;font-weight:900;margin:20px 0 12px;color:#e9e6d4;text-shadow:0 8px 30px #000b;transform:scaleX(1.04);transform-origin:left}
#screen-title h1 span{color:var(--amber)}
.title-sub{font-size:11px;letter-spacing:6px;color:#b9c6aa;margin-bottom:22px}
.blurb{font-size:11px;line-height:1.9;color:#a8b79b;max-width:470px;margin-bottom:26px}
.title-actions{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:28px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.title-stats{display:flex;gap:28px;padding-top:16px;border-top:1px solid var(--line);max-width:520px}
.title-stats>div{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px}
.title-stats span{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:2px;color:var(--dim)}
.title-stats b{font-size:11px;letter-spacing:1px;color:#d6e1c8;font-weight:600}
.title-side{position:absolute;right:5%;bottom:7%;z-index:2;text-align:right;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:12px;align-items:flex-end}
.quote{font-size:9px;line-height:1.8;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:#89977e;max-width:280px;text-align:right}
.pad-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;border:1px solid var(--line);padding:7px 10px;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:2px;color:var(--muted);background:rgba(9,15,10,.65)}
.pad-badge i{width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--dim);display:block}
.pad-badge.on i{background:var(--green);box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--green)}
.controls-strip{position:absolute;left:6.5%;bottom:5%;z-index:2;display:flex;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap;max-width:60%}
.controls-strip div{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:#7d8c71;display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center}
kbd{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:8px;background:#1b271b;border:1px solid #3d4e39;border-bottom-width:2px;padding:3px 5px;border-radius:2px;color:#d7e2c9}

/* ---------- panels / briefing ---------- */
.center-wrap{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;place-items:center;z-index:2}
.panel{background:linear-gradient(160deg,rgba(15,24,16,.97),rgba(8,13,9,.97));border:1px solid var(--line2);box-shadow:0 30px 80px #000b;position:relative}
.panel:before,.panel:after{content:"";position:absolute;width:14px;height:14px;border:1px solid var(--amber);opacity:.7;pointer-events:none}
.panel:before{left:-1px;top:-1px;border-right:0;border-bottom:0}
.panel:after{right:-1px;bottom:-1px;border-left:0;border-top:0}
.brief-frame{width:min(1040px,92%);padding:26px 30px 22px}
.brief-head{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:2.5px;color:var(--muted);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding-bottom:12px}
.brief-head b{color:var(--amber);font-weight:600}
.brief-frame h2{font-family:var(--display);font-size:52px;letter-spacing:2px;line-height:.9;margin:18px 0 4px;color:#e8e5d1}
.brief-sub{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:3px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:18px}
.brief-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.12fr .95fr;gap:22px}
.brief-map{position:relative;border:1px solid var(--line);background:#0a120c;overflow:hidden}
#briefMap{display:block;width:100%;height:auto;opacity:.9}
.map-label{position:absolute;left:9px;bottom:8px;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:2px;color:#829176;pointer-events:none}
.map-label.top{top:8px;bottom:auto}
.intel{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:0 18px;align-content:start}
.intel-row{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:10px;padding:8px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.08);font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.7px}
.intel-row span{color:var(--dim)}
.intel-row b{color:#dbe6ce;font-weight:500;text-align:right}
.intel-note{grid-column:1/-1;font-size:9px;line-height:1.85;color:#91a084;margin-top:12px;border-left:2px solid var(--amber);padding-left:10px}
.loadout-row{display:flex;gap:0;border:1px solid var(--line);margin-top:18px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.02)}
.loadout-cell{flex:1;padding:9px 12px;border-right:1px solid var(--line)}
.loadout-cell:last-child{border-right:0}
.loadout-cell span{display:block;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:2px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:4px}
.loadout-cell b{font-size:10px;color:#dbe6ce;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:.5px}
.brief-actions{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;margin-top:18px}
.brief-actions .right{display:flex;gap:9px}
.diff-pips{display:flex;gap:3px;align-items:center;margin-left:12px}
.diff-pips i{display:block;width:12px;height:4px;background:#2b3627}
.diff-pips i.on{background:var(--amber)}

/* ---------- armory ---------- */
.armory-frame{width:min(1180px,95%);height:min(650px,90%);padding:22px 24px;display:flex;flex-direction:column}
.armory-head{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-end;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding-bottom:12px;margin-bottom:14px}
.armory-head h2{font-family:var(--display);font-size:34px;letter-spacing:3px;line-height:.9;margin-top:4px}
.armory-credits{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:2px;color:var(--muted)}
.armory-credits b{color:var(--amber2);font-size:15px;font-weight:600;margin-left:6px}
.armory-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:250px 1fr 300px;gap:16px;flex:1;min-height:0}
.army-col{display:flex;flex-direction:column;min-height:0}
.army-label{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:2.5px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:8px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between}
.rifle-item{border:1px solid var(--line);background:rgba(255,255,255,.018);padding:10px 11px;margin-bottom:7px;cursor:pointer;transition:.14s;position:relative}
.rifle-item:hover{border-color:var(--line2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.035)}
.rifle-item.sel{border-color:var(--amber);background:linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(229,180,91,.11),rgba(229,180,91,.02))}
.rifle-item.locked{opacity:.62}
.rifle-item .rname{font-size:10px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:#dfe9d2;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:6px}
.rifle-item .rname em{font-style:normal;font-size:7px;color:var(--amber);letter-spacing:1px}
.rifle-item .rsub{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--dim);margin-top:4px}
.rifle-item .rprice{position:absolute;right:10px;bottom:8px;font-size:8px;color:var(--green)}
.rifle-item.selected-rifle:after{content:"EQUIPPED";position:absolute;right:9px;top:9px;font-size:6px;letter-spacing:1px;color:#111a0f;background:var(--amber);padding:2px 4px}
.detail-col{border-left:1px solid var(--line);border-right:1px solid var(--line);padding:0 18px;overflow-y:auto;scrollbar-width:thin}
.detail-col::-webkit-scrollbar{width:5px}.detail-col::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb{background:#3c4c37}
.dname{font-family:var(--display);font-size:31px;letter-spacing:2px;line-height:.95;color:#e9e6d3}
.dcal{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:3px;color:var(--amber);margin:5px 0 10px}
.ddesc{font-size:9px;line-height:1.8;color:#94a387;margin-bottom:14px;min-height:32px}
.statline{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin:6px 0;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1px;color:var(--muted)}
.statline span{width:54px;flex:none}
.statbar{flex:1;height:4px;background:#202a1d;overflow:hidden}
.statbar i{display:block;height:100%;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#7c9e6d,var(--amber))}
.statline b{width:56px;text-align:right;font-weight:500;color:#d5e0c8;font-size:8px}
.upgrade-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;padding:8px 0;border-top:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.08);font-size:8px}
.upgrade-row .un{flex:1}
.upgrade-row .un small{display:block;color:var(--dim);font-size:7px;letter-spacing:.4px;margin-top:3px}
.pips{display:flex;gap:2px;margin-right:4px}
.pips i{width:8px;height:8px;border:1px solid #4a5b43;background:#1a2417;display:block}
.pips i.on{background:var(--amber);border-color:var(--amber)}
.upbuy{border:1px solid var(--line2);padding:5px 7px;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1px;color:#cbd8bf;background:rgba(255,255,255,.03);min-width:58px}
.upbuy:hover{border-color:var(--amber);color:var(--amber2)}
.upbuy:disabled{opacity:.3}
.comp-card{border:1px solid rgba(229,180,91,.35);background:rgba(229,180,91,.05);padding:9px;margin-top:14px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:10px;align-items:center}
.comp-card .ct{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--amber2)}
.comp-card small{display:block;font-size:7px;line-height:1.6;color:#8d9b80;margin-top:3px}
.ammo-item{border:1px solid var(--line);padding:8px 9px;margin-bottom:6px;cursor:pointer;font-size:8px}
.ammo-item:hover{border-color:var(--line2)}
.ammo-item.sel{border-color:var(--green);background:rgba(143,211,154,.06)}
.ammo-item.locked{opacity:.6}
.ammo-item .an{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;color:#d8e4cc;letter-spacing:1px}
.ammo-item .an em{font-style:normal;color:var(--green);font-size:7px}
.ammo-item .as{color:var(--dim);font-size:7px;line-height:1.55;margin-top:3px}
.ammo-item .ap{float:right;color:var(--amber);font-size:7px;margin-top:2px}
.armory-foot{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;border-top:1px solid var(--line);padding-top:12px;margin-top:12px}
.hintline{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.4px;color:var(--dim)}

/* ---------- debrief ---------- */
.debrief-frame{width:min(700px,90%);padding:32px 36px 26px;text-align:center}
.debrief-kicker{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:5px;color:var(--green)}
.debrief-kicker.fail{color:var(--red)}
.debrief-frame h2{font-family:var(--display);font-size:44px;letter-spacing:2px;margin:8px 0 2px;color:#eae6d2}
.debrief-sub{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:3px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:20px}
.stat-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);border:1px solid var(--line);background:rgba(255,255,255,.015);margin-bottom:16px}
.stat-grid>div{padding:12px 8px;border-right:1px solid var(--line)}
.stat-grid>div:last-child{border-right:0}
.stat-grid span{display:block;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:5px}
.stat-grid b{font-size:18px;font-weight:500;color:#e0ead4}
.stat-grid b small{font-size:8px;color:var(--muted);margin-left:2px}
.reward-list{text-align:left;border-top:1px solid var(--line);padding-top:8px;margin-bottom:18px}
.reward-line{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1px;padding:4px 0;color:#96a489}
.reward-line.total{color:var(--amber2);border-top:1px solid var(--line);margin-top:6px;padding-top:9px;font-size:10px}
.debrief-actions{display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:10px}

/* ---------- hud ---------- */
#hud{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:10;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;transition:opacity .4s}
#hud.on{opacity:1}
.hud-top{position:absolute;left:18px;right:18px;top:15px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;gap:14px}
.hpanel{background:linear-gradient(160deg,rgba(8,14,9,.82),rgba(8,14,9,.58));border:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.2);padding:9px 12px;backdrop-filter:blur(3px)}
.mission-panel{min-width:190px}
.mission-panel .hud-opname{font-family:var(--display);font-size:20px;letter-spacing:2px;line-height:1;color:#e4e7d4;margin:4px 0 7px}
.target-row{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--muted)}
.target-row b{color:var(--amber2);font-weight:500}
.hud-center{text-align:center;padding-top:1px;min-width:190px}
.timer{font-size:27px;letter-spacing:3px;font-weight:500;color:#e6ead8;text-shadow:0 2px 8px #000;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.timer.warn{color:var(--red)}
.objective{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:2.5px;color:#93a287;margin-top:2px}
.wind-panel{min-width:178px;text-align:right}
.wind-main{display:flex;align-items:baseline;justify-content:flex-end;gap:5px;margin:3px 0 2px}
.wind-arrow{display:inline-block;font-size:16px;line-height:1;color:var(--amber2);transition:transform .2s;transform-origin:50% 50%}
.wind-speed{font-size:18px;color:#e4ead6;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.wind-main small{font-size:7px;color:var(--dim);letter-spacing:1px}
.wind-dir{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--muted)}
.weather-line{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.2px;color:var(--dim);margin-top:5px;border-top:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.1);padding-top:4px}
#feed{position:absolute;left:20px;top:104px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;width:290px}
.feed-item{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1px;line-height:1.5;color:#b8c8aa;background:rgba(6,11,7,.58);border-left:2px solid #5b6d52;padding:4px 7px;animation:feedin .2s ease}
.feed-item.good{border-left-color:var(--green);color:#cde5c1}
.feed-item.kill{border-left-color:var(--amber);color:#f2dec0}
.feed-item.bad{border-left-color:var(--red);color:#e4b8ac}
@keyframes feedin{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(-8px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}
.hud-bottom{position:absolute;left:18px;right:18px;bottom:16px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-end;gap:12px}
.weapon-panel{min-width:220px}
.weapon-name{font-family:var(--display);font-size:21px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:#e7e9d8;line-height:1}
.weapon-sub{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--dim);margin:4px 0 7px}
.ammo-line{display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:3px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
#hudAmmo{font-size:24px;color:var(--amber2);line-height:1}
.ammo-slash{font-size:12px;color:#617057;margin:0 1px}
#hudMag{font-size:12px;color:#9daa90}
.reload-hint{margin-left:auto;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1px;color:var(--red);opacity:0;transition:.2s}
.reload-hint.on{opacity:1;animation:blink 1s infinite}
@keyframes blink{50%{opacity:.25}}
.reload-bar{height:3px;background:#202a1d;margin-top:5px;overflow:hidden}
.reload-bar i{display:block;height:100%;width:100%;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#8ba978,var(--amber));transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left}
.ballistics-panel{min-width:230px}
.ball-row{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:1.4px;color:var(--dim);padding:3px 0}
.ball-row b{color:#dbe6ce;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:.6px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.ball-foot{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;border-top:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.12);margin-top:5px;padding-top:5px;font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.3px;color:var(--muted)}
#hudSolve{color:var(--amber)}
.stance-panel{min-width:190px;text-align:right}
.breath-label{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.8px;color:var(--dim)}
.breath-label span{color:#dbe6ce}
.breath-bar{height:4px;background:#202a1d;margin:6px 0 7px;overflow:hidden}
.breath-bar i{display:block;height:100%;width:100%;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#6fa783,#a9d58e);transform-origin:left}
.stance-hint{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1.4px;color:var(--amber);margin-bottom:3px}
.control-hint{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1px;color:var(--dim);line-height:1.7}
#hitmarker{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;width:38px;height:38px;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) rotate(45deg);opacity:0;pointer-events:none}
#hitmarker i{position:absolute;background:#fff;box-shadow:0 0 8px #fff}
#hitmarker i:nth-child(1){left:50%;top:0;width:2px;height:10px;transform:translateX(-50%)}
#hitmarker i:nth-child(2){left:50%;bottom:0;width:2px;height:10px;transform:translateX(-50%)}
#hitmarker i:nth-child(3){top:50%;left:0;height:2px;width:10px;transform:translateY(-50%)}
#hitmarker i:nth-child(4){top:50%;right:0;height:2px;width:10px;transform:translateY(-50%)}
#hitmarker.show{animation:hit .28s ease-out}
#hitmarker.head i{background:var(--amber2);box-shadow:0 0 10px var(--amber)}
@keyframes hit{0%{opacity:1;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) rotate(45deg) scale(.6)}100%{opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) rotate(45deg) scale(1.5)}}
#scopePrompt{position:absolute;left:50%;bottom:112px;transform:translateX(-50%);font-size:8px;letter-spacing:2px;color:#cfdcc0;background:rgba(6,11,7,.72);border:1px solid var(--line);padding:6px 12px;opacity:0;transition:.3s;white-space:nowrap}
#scopePrompt.on{opacity:1}
#banner{position:absolute;left:50%;top:39%;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);text-align:center;opacity:0;pointer-events:none;transition:opacity .2s}
#banner .b1{font-family:var(--display);font-size:46px;letter-spacing:5px;color:#f0e6c8;line-height:.9;text-shadow:0 3px 16px #000}
#banner .b2{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:4px;color:var(--amber);margin-top:6px}
#banner.on{opacity:1;animation:bannerin .3s ease-out}
@keyframes bannerin{from{opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(.94)}to{opacity:1;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1)}}
#floaters{position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none;overflow:hidden}
.floater{position:absolute;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:1.5px;color:var(--amber2);text-shadow:0 2px 6px #000;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);animation:floatup 1.3s ease-out forwards;white-space:nowrap}
.floater.red{color:#e98a6f}
@keyframes floatup{0%{opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,-40%) scale(.9)}15%{opacity:1}100%{opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,-160%) scale(1)}}
#slowmo{position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;background:radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 50%,transparent 35%,rgba(229,180,91,.14) 100%);transition:opacity .2s}
#slowmo.on{opacity:1}

/* ---------- pause ---------- */
#screen-pause .center-wrap{z-index:3}
.pause-frame{width:min(520px,90%);padding:28px 32px;text-align:center}
.pause-frame h2{font-family:var(--display);font-size:40px;letter-spacing:4px;margin-bottom:4px}
.pause-sub{font-size:8px;letter-spacing:3px;color:var(--dim);margin-bottom:20px}
.pause-actions{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px}
.pause-actions .btn{padding:11px 18px}
.pause-keys{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:5px 14px;margin-top:18px;text-align:left}
.pause-keys div{font-size:7px;letter-spacing:1px;color:#8c9b80;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(213,230,195,.07);padding:3px 0}
.pause-keys b{color:#c7d4ba;font-weight:500}
.mute-row{display:flex;justify-content:center;margin-top:12px}

@media (max-width:900px){
  #screen-title .title-wrap{width:74%}
  .title-side,.controls-strip{display:none}
  .brief-frame{padding:18px}.brief-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}.brief-map{display:none}
  .armory-frame{height:94%;padding:14px}.armory-grid{grid-template-columns:190px 1fr}.army-col.ammo-col{display:none}
  .hud-bottom{gap:6px}.weapon-panel{min-width:160px}.ballistics-panel{min-width:170px}.stance-panel{display:none}
  #feed{display:none}.hud-top{left:10px;right:10px;top:9px}.hud-bottom{left:10px;right:10px;bottom:9px}
}
</style>

<body>

## Objective
- Complete and validate LONGSHOT — Ballistic Overwatch, a playable sniper simulation with adjustable ballistics, optional gamepad controls, mission progression, rifles, and upgrades.

## Requirements
- Deliver without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save validation screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a single-page canvas game with first-person aiming, scope and ballistic tools, missions, career/armory progression, and keyboard/gamepad input.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game and prior fixes for aiming geometry, miss feedback, wind transformation, rifle equipping, career reset, and gamepad menu controls.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation with `node --check`.
- Browser-checked title, briefing, deployment, HUD, scope, and terrain rangefinding; no browser console errors reported.
- Reset local storage and confirmed a fresh career starts with 250 credits and the M24 equipped.

### Active
- Validate consistent target acquisition and hits, armory progression, and gamepad/menu input.
- Save a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg` (maximum width 1280px) and inspect only that latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- Target hit validation remains unresolved: firing at a manually aimed, ranged target did not register a hit; aim/view state may be drifting or ballistic correction/target geometry may be misaligned.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose aim/view drift and verify shooting through the intended gameplay inputs; establish a reliable target hit.
2. Continue validating armory progression and gamepad/menu interactions.
3. Save and inspect a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg`.
4. Summarize implementation and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation; modified and uncommitted.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Existing title-screen screenshot; must be replaced with a fresh validation capture.
- `Agents.md`: Modified and uncommitted.

## Important Context
- Browser server is running at `http://localhost:3002`; browser session is open.
- `window.GAME` exposes test helpers including `deploy`, `aimAt`, `setScope`, `fire`, `range`, and `solve`.
- Manual aim changes may be overwritten by `updateView()` deriving actual view from aim plus sway/recoil; `aimAt()` sets aim values but does not freeze view.
- `GAME.range()` found a target when the view was manually aligned, but a subsequent test aimed at sloped terrain and returned `LASER · TERRAIN`; direct firing tests showed no kill and misses.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

## Objective
- Complete and validate LONGSHOT — Ballistic Overwatch, a playable sniper simulation with adjustable ballistics, optional gamepad controls, mission progression, rifles, and upgrades.

## Requirements
- Deliver without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save validation screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a single-page canvas game with first-person aiming, scope and ballistic tools, missions, career/armory progression, and keyboard/gamepad input.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game and prior fixes for aiming geometry, miss feedback, wind transformation, rifle equipping, career reset, and gamepad menu controls.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation with `node --check`.
- Browser-checked title, briefing, deployment, HUD, scope, and terrain rangefinding; no browser console errors reported.
- Reset local storage and confirmed a fresh career starts with 250 credits and the M24 equipped.
- Confirmed a repeatable elimination using a stationary target at 190m, `GAME.range()`, `GAME.solve()`, and `GAME.fire()`.

### Active
- Diagnose why firing at a normal mission target after `GAME.aimAt(0)` and applying a ballistic solution can still miss; one test returned `MISS · RIGHT`.
- Validate armory progression and gamepad/menu input.
- Save a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg` (maximum width 1280px) and inspect only that latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- Reliable acquisition and hit registration on naturally generated targets remain unverified; stationary controlled-target testing succeeds, but a normal-target shot missed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect firing direction, ballistic correction, target motion, and hitboxes to explain the normal-target `MISS · RIGHT`.
2. Establish and verify a repeatable hit using ordinary gameplay inputs and generated targets.
3. Validate armory progression and gamepad/menu interactions.
4. Save and inspect a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg`, no wider than 1280px.
5. Summarize implementation and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation; modified and uncommitted.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Existing screenshot to replace with a fresh validation capture.

## Important Context
- Browser server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; browser session is open.
- `window.GAME` exposes `deploy`, `aimAt`, `aimAtPoint`, `setScope`, `fire`, `range`, and `solve`.
- Relevant code: `fireShot()` at `index.html:1581`, `stepBullet()` at `1634`, hitboxes at `1680`, `updateView()` at `2016`, `rangeFind()` at `1917`, and `applySolution()` at `1952`.
- `GAME.aimAt()` aligns view to approximate chest height. Rangefinding can acquire the target, but a natural-target shot after range/solve missed right; a controlled stationary target at 190m was eliminated with the same firing pipeline.
- `index.html` changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete and validate LONGSHOT — Ballistic Overwatch, a playable sniper simulation with adjustable ballistics, optional gamepad controls, mission progression, rifles, and upgrades.

## Requirements
- Deliver without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save validation screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a single-page canvas game with first-person aiming, scope and ballistic tools, missions, career/armory progression, and keyboard/gamepad input.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game and prior fixes for aiming geometry, miss feedback, wind transformation, rifle equipping, career reset, and gamepad menu controls.
- JavaScript syntax check passed using an extracted script saved to `/tmp/opencode/game-check.js`.
- Browser-checked title, briefing, deployment, HUD, scope, and terrain rangefinding; no console errors were reported previously.
- Confirmed fresh career starts with 250 credits and the M24 equipped.
- Confirmed ballistic range-and-solve firing can eliminate a stationary target at 190–196m.

### Active
- Validate hits on naturally generated targets; recent normal-target shots still failed to confirm a hit, with one reporting `MISS · RIGHT`.
- Validate armory progression and gamepad/menu interactions.
- Save a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg` (maximum width 1280px) and inspect only that latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- Repeatable hits on naturally moving/generated targets remain unverified; stationary controlled-target testing succeeds, while natural-target tests missed or did not confirm a kill.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose and test aim/range/solution alignment and bullet arrival against a naturally generated target.
2. Validate armory progression and gamepad/menu interactions.
3. Capture a fresh JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg`, ensure it is no wider than 1280px, and inspect only that screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation, validation, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation; modified and uncommitted.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Existing JPEG to replace with a fresh validation capture.

## Important Context
- Browser server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; browser session remains open.
- `window.GAME` exposes `deploy`, `aimAt`, `aimAtPoint`, `setScope`, `fire`, `range`, and `solve`.
- Generated static targets oscillate around `baseX`; walking and runner targets move. A frozen generated target hit at 196m, but normal generated-target shots have missed.
- `git status` showed `Agents.md` and `index.html` modified; changes are uncommitted.

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version
